A welcome screen, a Start menu entry, and automatic updates.

**Download `iconger.exe` below.** This is the last update you'll need to download by hand: from here on, Iconger updates itself.

## New
- **Updates itself.** When Iconger opens, it checks GitHub for a newer version. A small line at the bottom left of the sidebar shows what's happening, and if there's an update, Iconger shows what's new and asks before installing it. Say yes, and it downloads the new version, checks it isn't damaged (size and SHA-256), swaps it in and restarts. Turn it off, or check by hand, in **Settings → Updates and Start menu**.
- **Find it in Windows search.** Iconger adds itself to the Start menu, so you can search "Iconger" and pin it like any other app. If you move `iconger.exe`, the shortcut follows it the next time you open Iconger. You can remove it in Settings.
- **Welcome screen.** The first time you open Iconger, it explains the three steps and lets you choose the two options above. If you've used Iconger before, you won't see it.

Your backups and settings carry over.
